subject: Unexplained burst on June 20 invoice and collections timeline
messages:
From: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@farsight.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Farsight Finance Team <finance@farsight.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike on Jun 20 — requesting explanation and collection hold

Hi Olga,

We received the June invoice this morning and noticed a ~6.2x usage spike on June 20 compared to our average. Attached is a short CSV with the hourly counts we see on our side (usage_sample_20270620.csv). The spike appears to correspond to a batch job that should have been routed to our staging keys; we only ran a single deploy that day.

Can you confirm whether this was counted on a single API key and whether there are any known bulk-replay events from your ingest pipeline between 2027-06-20 02:00–06:00 UTC? We need to decide whether to hold payment for the disputed amount while we investigate — please advise on the collection hold process and what evidence you can provide (raw telemetry snippet, per-request ids, or a usage export).

We’ve attached the invoice (invoice_202706.pdf) as well. Our payments team is pausing the wire until we get an explanation or a provisional credit.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround, Alicia

--
Alicia Grant
Head of Finance, Farsight AI
Alicia.Grant@farsight.ai

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@farsight.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike on Jun 20 — requesting explanation and collection hold

Hi Alicia — thanks for flagging and for the CSV. I’ve started an internal triage and put Ben (billing ops) and Kim (account rep) on copy. Initial notes:

- We see an elevated token count in our aggregate logs for the same window (02:10–05:40 UTC).
- Preliminary correlation shows requests originating from your primary org id but spread across three API keys.
- We’re gathering the per-request ids and a raw telemetry snippet; attaching what we have so far (raw-telemetry-snippet.txt).

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) Ben will pull a per-request export for the 02:00–06:00 UTC window and check for replay/duplicate request ids.
2) I’ll validate key ownership mapping in our key registry to see whether a staging key was mis-tagged.
3) Kim will coordinate the collections timeline and confirm a provisional credit policy for suspected ingestion anomalies.

Ben / Kim — can you confirm ETA for the exports and whether we can offer a provisional credit to unfreeze their payment? Alicia — can you confirm if you pushed any large batched jobs that day or rotated keys?

Appreciate the patience — we’ll be back with a more concrete breakdown within the day.

Best,
Olga
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@farsight.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike on Jun 20 — requesting explanation and collection hold

Thanks, Olga. I pulled the per-request export and attached a short subset (see attachment: usage_sample_20270620.csv). Quick findings:
- 04:01:12–04:12:43 UTC: a tight cluster of 9,300 requests with identical client_request_id and identical prompt hashes spread across three API keys (key-A, key-C, key-draft).
- The KV cache miss rate was unusually high for that timeframe indicating a cold-start pattern consistent with parallel replay.
- There are multiple identical session ids that differ only by a suffix; looks like a bulk replay from an ingestion pipeline rather than normal live traffic.

Given this pattern, I recommend a provisional credit for the duplicate clusters while we finish a rule-based scrub to reclassify replayed requests. Policy note: for suspected ingestion/replay where we can identify duplicate request ids and apply dedup, we typically offer a provisional 60% credit pending final forensic confirmation (up to our discretion).

Kim — if we offer a provisional credit, can you outline the collections hold wording so Farsight’s AP team can proceed with the payment hold? Alicia — if you prefer, we can also provide a filtered export that removes the deduped rows so you can reconcile locally.

- Ben
Director, Billing Operations

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@farsight.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike on Jun 20 — requesting explanation and collection hold

Hi Alicia,

Thanks for raising this and for pausing payment while we investigate. Per our standard collections process for disputed usage:

1) We can mark the disputed line item as "provisionally credited" which pauses further collections on that amount for up to 30 days while forensic work completes.
2) To proceed I need a short confirmation from your AP team (one-line reply to this thread) that they will hold the wire for the disputed amount and the expected contact person for release.
3) Once Ben completes the dedup scrub I’ll issue a provisional credit (60% on the duplicated volume) and send a revised invoice so your AP can pull the updated amount for payment.

If you prefer a quicker route, we can also issue a temporary invoice adjustment (credit memo) today and follow up with a final reconciliation later — whichever is easiest for your internal procurement. Let me know which option you prefer.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@farsight.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike on Jun 20 — requesting explanation and collection hold

Thanks all — Farsight AP confirms they will hold the wire for the disputed portion. Contact: Marco Li (marco.li@farsight.ai). We prefer the provisional credit + revised invoice route so we can close month-end on time.

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the offer of a filtered export — please send the deduped usage CSV and the proposed credit memo when ready. We’ll unlock payment once we receive the revised invoice.

Best,
Alicia
--
Alicia Grant
Head of Finance, Farsight AI
